week_in_history.narrative:
This week's dusty VHS pull comes from 2023, Week 4 — the closest margin of any Week 4 game in the history of this league, with Brian Harris's Tomahawk Piranhas edging John Schauder's Nicebois by a microscopic 1.82 points. That's the kind of loss that should rattle around a man's skull for a decade, and judging by what came next, it did.

Brian limped out of that nail-biter and played .500 ball the rest of the way at 5-5, somehow backing into the playoffs anyway, where the Piranhas promptly flamed out in the quarterfinal — proof that squeaking out a win by less than two points doesn't exactly build championship DNA.

Meanwhile John took that 106.2 gut-punch and never recovered, cratering to a 3-6 finish and missing the playoffs entirely. One point eighty-two separated "mediocre but alive" from "watching from the couch," and John spent the rest of that season finding out which one he was.

stat_of_the_week.narrative: The historical chance of making the playoffs if you are 0-3. Since 2023, 4 teams have started 0-3: Andrew Williams (2023), Brian Harris (2024), Daniel Bahamonde (2025), Eddie McCumiskey (2025). None of them went on to make the playoffs.

weekly_recap.previous_weekend:
Final score: Greg Wigton 104.04, Kevin Mallon 98.78, a margin of 5.26 points — the kind of nail-biter that makes you wonder why either of these men bothered getting out of bed to set a lineup. This is their third all-time meeting, and Wigton extends the all-time series lead to 2-0, because apparently this matchup is just his personal hobby alongside being, per league record, really really good looking.

Jordan Love's 20.48 points gave Kevin something to brag about, right up until Trey Smack face-planted for 1.0 points and dragged the whole roster down with him. Lamar Jackson matched him nearly point for point with 20.44 for Greg, while Isaiah Likely quietly did nothing useful at 2.3. Saquon Barkley's 8.5 points in the final game sealed Kevin's fate outright. And somebody on Kevin's bench, Harold Fannin Jr., sat there with 20.6 points while Tre Tucker's 6.3 played starter — a 14.3-point gift that would've flipped this game. Kevin's 41.2% career winning percentage remains tragically consistent with his lineup management.
weekly_recap.honorable_mention: This week's biggest blowout came with a gruesome score attached: 124.3 to 64.34, a 59.96-point massacre that left Jason Carlton's roster looking like it got hit by a truck. Sixty-four points isn't a fantasy score, it's a cry for help — and his 49ers D/ST turning in a flat 0.0 points is the kind of contribution you'd expect from a card he ripped and immediately threw in the trash. Meanwhile Josh Davis rode Jahmyr Gibbs's 37.9-point explosion to a laugher. The series is tied 1-1 all-time, but with a career winning percentage of 61.3% now sporting this ugly footnote, Carlton's trading card luck clearly doesn't extend to Sundays.
weekly_recap.game_of_the_week: John Schauder brings his Nicebois into this one ranked 9th with a 1-2 record, and the nickname is doing a lot of charity work given his career 33.3 winning percentage and a career resume that reads zero playoff appearances, zero championships through three complete seasons — truly the "always the bridesmaid" guy, which his own background note admits, standing there holding a bouquet while everyone else gets rings. Carl Bruce, meanwhile, sits ranked 4th at 2-1, averaging 115.99 points a game this season to John's 103.43, and actually owns a career championship to go with his career 53.3 winning percentage. John does hold the all-time series lead 2-1, so Carl's trophy case apparently doesn't open for him specifically. Carl's playoff odds improved from 63.3% to 63.3% this week, still comfortably ahead of John's climb from 47.9% to 47.9%. History favors John; math favors Carl's couch.
